headline: Deferred approval of fiscal 2026 annual report pending member edits; no standing clerk will be elected.
summary: Members gave updates on the Green Community Festival, the director search, and strategic plan working groups. Approval of the FY2026 annual report was deferred until edits are sent before the next meeting. A minute taker will be designated at each meeting instead of electing a clerk.
decisions: Approved the draft minutes of August 11, 2026.
Decided not to elect a standing clerk; a clerk or minute taker will be designated at the start of each meeting.
Deferred approval of the FY2026 annual report until edits and comments are submitted before the next meeting.
Moved the committee photo from September to the October meeting, scheduled for about 6:15 to 6:20 PM.

plain_text:
Page 1 
Economic Development Committee 
September 8, 2026  
The South Burlington Economic Development Committee held a regular meeting at 5:30 PM 
in Room 301 of the South Burlington City Hall, 180 Market Street, South Burlington and by 
remote participation.  
Members present:  Nicole LaBrecque (Chair), Chris Carrigan (Vice Chair), Harold 
Hershberg, Paige Brochu, John Burton, Emma Shouldice-Boardman, Rebecca Killian, Brad 
Krompf, Jason Mintz  
Members absent:  None. 
Also present:  Ilona Blanchard, South Burlington Community Development Director 
(Committee Staff), Andrew Chalnick, City Council (Council Liaison)  
1. The meeting was called to order by Nicole LaBrecque, Chair, at 5:30 p.m. Emergency 
exit procedures were reviewed. The Committee welcomed Jason as a new committee 
member. The agenda was approved (moved by Rebecca Killian, seconded by Emma 
Shouldice-Boardman) unanimously.  
2. Comments from the Public. No members of the public were present; no public comment 
was offered. 
3. Review and Approve Minutes from Prior Meetings 
a. August 11, 2026. The draft minutes were approved (moved by Emma Shouldice-
Boardman, seconded by Paige Brochu). 
4. Updates: 
a. Chair (Nicole LaBrecque):  
 Connected with Bettina regarding participation in the Green Community 
Festival (September 19); there is no more room for additional companies 
or organizations this year – strong interest from many. Members were 
asked to send Bettina the names of any additional organizations to 
consider for the future. 
 Second-round interviews are underway for the Economic Development 
Director position; Nicole has met one candidate already. The process is 
expected to conclude with a recommendation by September 9, with a 
name to be announced most likely by the next meeting.
Economic Development Committee Meeting Minutes | Page 2 
 Nicole has been assisting Beta Technologies with site planning and 
expansion. 
b. Staff (Ilona Blanchard): 
o Met with Hello Burlington to review credit card and phone-activity data 
using AI tools; prompts and questions can be submitted to help analyze 
hospitality-related data. The dataset covers a two-year period (June 2024 
– June 2026). Emma expressed interest in attending the next meeting. 
o Shared a breakdown of first-time versus repeat visitors to City Center. 
Notable findings: City Center draws more visitors than Burlington itself; 
City Center figures include Staples Plaza and University Mall. 
o UVM undergraduates have moved in; roughly 150 residents were using 
the bus stop at the Garden Street apartments daily last week. 
o Economic Mobility Initiative event: approximately 30 people attended, 
including many service providers and entrepreneurs. Discussion touched 
on how the City is reaching out to communities, what opportunities exist 
with various communities, and career development / untapped potential. 
c. Member Committee Activities (Paige and Chris): 
o UVM has launched a new, statewide Division of Economic 
Development. This may create an opportunity for the South Burlington 
EDC to participate around messaging and coordination with UVM and 
communities across the state. 
o Leahy Center is conducting a listening session with communities. 
o Noted that the Burlington Business Association (BBA) has dissolved and 
that the Chamber plans to build an association. 
d. Council (Andrew): 
o Quality of Life Ordinance (“empowering public safety with 
compassion”): addresses tents on public land and solicitors on medians. 
The ordinance would make it illegal to set up a tent on public property 
or to stand on a median, with the intent of using ordinance and 
compassion together to improve quality of life in South Burlington. 
Andrew noted there is an economic development impact associated with 
this issue. 
o E-bikes that function as motorcycles: new authority will allow 
enforcement of speed and vehicle rules on bike paths. 
o Noise ordinance enforcement is an ongoing issue with motorcycles 
operating without mufflers in downtown Burlington. 
5. Officer Elections
Economic Development Committee Meeting Minutes | Page 3 
Elect Clerk: The Committee decided (no formal action needed) that a standing Clerk will 
not be elected; instead, a clerk/minute taker will be designated at the start of each meeting 
going forward.  
6. Economic Development Strategic Plan 
a. Work Session: How to Tell the Story to the Community – Communicating Plan/Rollout.  
b. Working Groups Report: 
• Innovation District and Aviation Sector: Noted an uptick in mergers and acquisitions 
activity, with discussion of pursuing such mergers in a sustainable way. 
• Hospitality/Destination: The working group plans to write up its thinking into an 
onboarding-style document/approach. 
• Permit Expediting/Concierge Permitting Concept: Continuing to test the process with 
Beta Technologies, meeting with the City every couple of weeks and bringing in 
Planning, Zoning, Public Works, and other departments. This approach is already 
being piloted through the Beta Technologies Master Plan process.  
• The working group structure may be reimagined once the new Executive Director is 
in place. Frameworks need to be drafted by October. 
7. Annual Report FY2026 
a. Review Draft Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2026 (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026). The 
draft was circulated at the meeting. The Committee will submit edits/comments before 
the next meeting; edits noted during discussion included: 
• Update Chris Carrigan's term end date to 2028. 
• Strategic Plan Implementation, 2nd bullet (Innovation District and Aviation): add 
reference to SBBA, UVM, and area businesses.  
• Regional Collaboration: revise the “removing systemic barriers” language to 
specifically reference economic mobility (i.e., “removing systemic barriers to 
upward economic mobility”). 
• Add language welcoming all new businesses to City Center, not solely Leunig's. 
b. Approval was deferred pending the Committee's edits and comments, to be submitted 
before the next meeting. 
8. Other Business
Economic Development Committee Meeting Minutes | Page 4 
9. Adjournment 
The meeting was adjourned (moved by Harold Hershberg, seconded by Emma Shouldice-
Boardman/John Burton). 
Paige Brochu
